say.en: If a company receives 95 rupees today but must repay 110 rupees later, it has a loss of 15 rupees on each debenture. Where does that loss go? In this lesson: Record the six cases of issue and redemption terms.
Write off discount or loss on issue.
Record interest on debentures.

body.en: Six cases: (1) issued at par, redeemable at par; (2) at discount, redeemable at par; (3) at premium, redeemable at par; (4) at par, redeemable at premium; (5) at discount, redeemable at premium; (6) at premium, redeemable at premium. When redemption is at a premium, debit Loss on *Issue* of Debentures A/c and credit Premium on Redemption of Debentures A/c (a liability) at the time of issue.
body.kn: ಸಾಲಪತ್ರಗಳನ್ನು ಅಧಿಮೌಲ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ವಿಮೋಚಿಸಬೇಕಾದರೆ, ವಿತರಣೆಯ ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲೇ ಆ ಅಧಿಮೌಲ್ಯವನ್ನು ಜವಾಬ್ದಾರಿಯಾಗಿ ದಾಖಲಿಸಿ, ವಿತರಣಾ ನಷ್ಟ ಖಾತೆಗೆ ಖರ್ಚು ಹಾಕಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: Writing off the loss and recording interest

body.en: Discount or loss on issue is written off first from Securities Premium; any balance is written off to the Statement of Profit and Loss as finance cost, in the year the debentures are allotted. *Interest*: Debenture Interest A/c Dr, To Debentureholders A/c; on payment Debentureholders A/c Dr, To Bank A/c; at year end transfer Debenture Interest to the Statement of Profit and Loss.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. Netravati Ltd. issued 1,000, 10 percent debentures of 100 rupees each at a discount of 5 percent, redeemable at a premium of 10 percent. Pass the entries on issue.
Cash received equals 1,000 times 95 rupees equals 95,000 rupees: Bank A over c Dr 95,000 rupees; To Debenture Application and Allotment A over c 95,000 rupees.
Loss on issue equals 5,000 rupees discount plus 10,000 rupees premium on redemption equals 15,000 rupees.

Debenture Application and Allotment A over c Dr 95,000 rupees; Loss on Issue of Debentures A over c Dr 15,000 rupees; To 10 percent Debentures A over c 1,00,000 rupees; To Premium on Redemption of Debentures A over c 10,000 rupees.
Check: debits 1,10,000 rupees equals credits 1,10,000 rupees.
So the answer is Loss on issue 15,000 rupees; Premium on Redemption liability 10,000 rupees.

problem.en: A company has ₹2,00,000, 9% debentures; interest is paid half-yearly on 30 September and 31 March. Find each payment and the annual charge.

steps.en: At year end: Statement of Profit and Loss Dr ₹18,000; To Debenture Interest A/c ₹18,000.

answer.en: ₹9,000 every six months; ₹18,000 charged as finance cost.

narration.en: Let us work this out together, step by step.

say.en: Let us work this out together, step by step. A company has 2,00,000, rupees 9 percent debentures; interest is paid half-yearly on 30 September and 31 March. Find each payment and the annual charge.
Annual interest equals 9 percent of 2,00,000 rupees equals 18,000 rupees.
Each half-yearly payment equals 18,000 rupees divided by 2 equals 9,000 rupees.
At year end: Statement of Profit and Loss Dr 18,000 rupees; To Debenture Interest A over c 18,000 rupees.
So the answer is 9,000 rupees every six months; 18,000 rupees charged as finance cost.
